**Proof idea.** Let `a = log g1`, `b = log g2`, and `F(x) = sSup_s exp(x·a(s) + b(s))`. The left-hand side equals `F(x)`, which is convex and finite because `a` and `b` are bounded.

- For each `t`, `m(t)` is the left derivative of `F` at `t`, defined as a sup of slopes. Convexity gives the supporting-line inequality `F(t) + m(t)(z − t) ≤ F(z)` for all `z`.
- Take `h1 = m` and `h2(t) = F(t) − t·m(t)`. Then `x·h1(t) + h2(t) = F(t) + m(t)(x − t) ≤ F(x)`, with equality at `t = x`. So the right-hand sup equals `F(x)`.
